Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s “FINAL” labels and assertions that terms are standard, agreed or not to be reopened are negotiation positions, not binding instructions or evidence of Buyer agreement. The draft package also contains internal mismatches: it says the Riverlark facility will be released after Completion although the disclosure says it remains outstanding with no discharge; it says the Bluefen consent is addressed although no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is included; and the disclosed bonuses are missing from the funds flow. Do not accept the package as a balanced whole without reconciling those points.

### Priority pushbacks

1. **Price, debt-free/cash-free mechanics and completion funds flow.** The Riverlark facility is approximately **$3.2m** and is not repaid or discharged. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed to acquired debt and secured assets. Require repayment from Seller proceeds at Completion, a lender payout letter and executed releases/discharges as completion deliverables; retain enough purchase price in escrow if registration or confirmation necessarily follows. Reconcile the $24m price mechanics and funds flow so debt, cash and working-capital adjustments are explicit and not double-counted.

   The **$420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from the draft funds flow. Establish who bears the bonuses and related payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. If they are Seller-side value leakage or accrued liabilities, deduct them from proceeds or treat them as debt-like, with an appropriate adjustment for on-costs. Do not let “a matter for the Seller” leave the Company or Buyer paying an unpriced liability.

2. **Bluefen consent: a genuine condition, not an endeavours promise.** Bluefen represents about **30% of FY26 revenue**; its change-of-control clause has conditions, and no final consent or evidence those conditions are satisfied is disclosed. Make receipt of unconditional written consent **and satisfaction/waiver of all associated conditions** a condition precedent to Completion. “Reasonable endeavours” and delivery of a consent letter alone are insufficient if conditions remain. Provide a termination right or other meaningful remedy if consent is not obtained by a longstop date.

3. **Caps, thresholds and time bars are too seller-favourable as drafted.** A **$4.8m aggregate cap** (20% of price), a **$25,000 de minimis**, and a **$250,000 tipping basket** materially constrain recovery for ordinary warranty breaches, especially in combination. Push for a materially higher general cap, a lower per-claim de minimis and basket, and a **tipping** basket—once crossed, recover from the first dollar, not only the excess. Confirm related claims cannot be artificially split or aggregated in a way that disadvantages Buyer.

   Do not apply the general cap, basket or 18-month period across the board. Carve out title and capacity, fraud, deliberate concealment, and other appropriate fundamental claims from the general cap and ordinary time limit. Give tax claims a period aligned to the relevant tax assessment/claim period plus a buffer; give specific indemnities their own negotiated limits and survival periods. General warranty notice should be at least the proposed 18 months, with claims preserved if notified within the period and resolved later. The Seller’s proposal that all Claims inherit the same limitations unless expressly stated otherwise risks swallowing these distinctions.

4. **Knowledge, disclosure and reliance provisions threaten to gut the protection.** Reject a bar for anything the Buyer or its advisers “had knowledge” of, including matters merely discoverable in the data room or public records. At most, negotiate a narrowly defined, actual-knowledge qualification limited to specified individuals’ actual conscious awareness, excluding constructive or imputed knowledge, and only for matters fairly and specifically disclosed. Likewise, reject blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records: it makes the warranty package close to illusory and leaves uncertainty about what was disclosed. Require specific, fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and reasonably apparent scope of each matter. Preserve the agreed warranties and remedies; non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording must not bar fraud, specific indemnities, debt/price adjustments, or other express contractual remedies. Have counsel check the interaction of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 rather than assessing them in isolation.

5. **Ironquay: the existing indemnity may not protect the asset being acquired.** DD-004 says transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 records **$180,000 open**, but is not independent verification of non-payment, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. The Seller’s proposed indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment may not ensure the Company owns or can use the materials. Require evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment (and any necessary consents) at or before Completion, or a holdback/escrow and a specific indemnity covering title, infringement, non-transfer, replacement/transition costs and related losses—not just the invoice amount.

6. **Export/privacy incident needs investigation, protection and an informed decision.** DD-006 describes a download link sent to an unintended external address and potentially about **1,240 records**, but does not establish access, exact scope or notification obligations. Calling it preliminary or immaterial does not resolve the risk. Require the full incident file, prompt completion of the investigation, preservation of evidence, confirmation of access/scope and any required notifications or remediation, plus targeted privacy, data-security and incident warranties. Consider a specific indemnity for the incident and a completion condition or price/escrow protection if material uncertainty remains. Avoid treating the disclosure as either an admission of breach or an adequate cure.

### Other matters to address

- **Supplier renewals:** The three related renewals total **$330,000**. The disclosure does not establish whether they are terminable, accrued, unavoidable or ordinary-course. Obtain the contracts, renewal terms, termination rights and accrued amounts; assess whether these are ordinary operating costs or a commitment/value leakage requiring adjustment or specific protection.
- **Lease and Mossvale:** Do not assume the share sale itself triggers landlord or Mossvale consent: the disclosures say only that the lease has a notification obligation and Mossvale has an assignment restriction. Verify the full documents, identify any actual change-of-control trigger, and require any notice or consent that is in fact required.
- **Title:** DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares, but that is evidence relied on by Seller, not a substitute for Buyer verification or a complete title package. Require unqualified warranties on good title, full ownership and authority to transfer, free of encumbrances, plus original/correctly executed transfer documents and updated registers at Completion.
- **Tax and IP:** “Settled under the general regime” is not enough. Secure tailored tax warranties and a tax indemnity with an appropriate survival period and cap; ensure IP ownership, employee/contractor assignments, licences and infringement risks are specifically covered, including the Ironquay issue. Do not let general caps or blanket disclosure silently displace those protections.

## Recommended negotiating position

Make the critical protections operative in the SPA, not just in the Seller’s update: (1) no Completion without effective Bluefen consent and a Riverlark payoff/release arrangement; (2) reconcile the $24m debt-free/cash-free price and properly allocate the $420,000 bonuses and on-costs; (3) narrow general disclosure and knowledge qualifications; (4) improve the cap, basket and claim periods, with appropriate carve-outs; and (5) obtain targeted Ironquay and incident protections, plus tailored tax/IP coverage. Verify lease, Mossvale, supplier and share-title matters against the underlying documents. The disclosure letter expressly says it does not admit breach or liability; that reservation does not reduce the need to protect Buyer against the disclosed facts.
